newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares set record at open, seen up on flows.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares set record at open, seen up on flows.

text.p: Russian shares lifted to new records at the opening on Tuesday and traders said new long-term investors were buying and were likely to continue doing so.

Leading shares were seen attracting the most new money because of their relatively high liquidity and since less liquid stocks in the second tier recently have seen prices jump, decreasing their their desirability.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at a record 396.15, inching up on its record close on Monday of 369.00
Oil producer LUKoil LKOH.RTS rose to $16.14 from $15.97 regional power utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS rose to $1.294 from $1.277 at 0810 GMT on the RTS.
Ordinary and preferred shares of bank Sberbank SBER.RTS SBER_p.RTS eased slightly but saw high volume, trading at $232.00 after $233.00 and $3.80 after $3.95.
"It feels like the start of a trend," said Brunswick Director Martin Diggle. "There are more serious, longer-term investors."
Diggle predicted the market would continue up for the week, chiefly on first tier shares, leaving the RTS index a few percent up on current levels.
Traders said there were slightly more allocations from new investors than experienced ones.
"There are some decent reports coming out of the Annual General Meetings," said ING Barings chief equities trader Peter Kizenko. "Mosenergo has helped boost the market."

He said First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov's political prominence was easing lingering fears of finding a successor to President Boris Yeltsin, who was sick late last year and early this year, in a worst-case scenario.
Traders said investors were finding it difficult to find value stocks in the third and other echelons which could absorb substantial funds, leading some back to leading shares.
"At the end of the day if you have parcels of money, you have to look at the blue chips," Diggle said.
